items.stem: In the sentence 'The tall boy ran quickly.', which word is an adverb?

explain.why: 'tall' describes the noun 'boy', so it is an adjective
'boy' names a person, so it is a noun
'ran' is a doing word, so it is a verb

solution: 'quickly' tells how the boy ran, so it is an adverb.

items.stem: In the sentence 'Wei Jie kicked the ball.', which word is a verb?

explain.why: 'Wei Jie' names a person, so it is a noun
'the' is an article that introduces a noun
'ball' names a thing, so it is a noun

solution: 'kicked' is the action word, so it is a verb.

items.stem: In the sentence 'She bought a red umbrella.', which word is an adjective?

explain.why: 'bought' is an action, so it is a verb
'She' stands for a person, so it is a pronoun
'umbrella' names a thing, so it is a noun

solution: 'red' describes the umbrella, so it is an adjective.

items.stem: In the sentence 'I wanted to go out, but it was raining.', which word is a conjunction?

explain.why: 'out' tells where, so it is an adverb here
'wanted' is an action, so it is a verb
'raining' is a verb form

solution: 'but' joins two parts of the sentence, so it is a conjunction.

items.stem: Which tense is used in 'Mum cooked dinner last night.'?

explain.why: 'cooked' is a past form and 'last night' shows past time
there is no 'will', and 'last night' is already past
there is no 'is' or 'are' with an '-ing' verb

solution: 'cooked' and 'last night' show an action finished in the past.

items.stem: In the sentence 'Ben said that he was tired.', which word is a pronoun?

explain.why: 'Ben' is a name, so it is a noun
'said' is a doing word, so it is a verb
'tired' describes how Ben felt, so it is an adjective

solution: 'he' stands in for 'Ben', so it is a pronoun.

items.stem: In the sentence 'The book is on the table.', which word is a preposition?

explain.why: 'book' names a thing, so it is a noun
'is' is a verb
'table' names a thing, so it is a noun

solution: 'on' shows where the book is, so it is a preposition.

items.stem: Which tense is used in 'The children are playing in the park.'?

explain.why: 'are playing' is more than the simple present form
'are' is present, not 'were'
there is no 'will' in the sentence

solution: 'are' with 'playing' shows an action in progress now.

items.stem: In the sentence 'Although it was late, Ravi kept studying.', which word is a conjunction?

explain.why: 'late' describes the time, so it is an adjective
'kept' is a verb
'studying' is a verb form

solution: 'Although' joins the two clauses, so it is a conjunction.

items.stem: Which tense is used in 'She has finished her homework.'?

explain.why: 'has finished' uses 'has' with a past participle, not a simple past form
the past perfect uses 'had', not 'has'
there is no '-ing' verb in the sentence

solution: 'has' with 'finished' is the present perfect.

items.stem: In the sentence 'Ali is taller than Ben.', what kind of word is 'taller'?

explain.why: a superlative would end in '-est' and be used with 'the'
'taller' describes Ali, a noun, so it is not an adverb
'taller' describes a person and does not name one

solution: 'taller' compares two people, so it is a comparative adjective.

items.stem: In the sentence 'After school, Mei Ling feeds the stray cats.', which word is the subject?

explain.why: 'school' is part of the phrase 'After school', which tells when
'cats' is the object, receiving the action
'feeds' is the verb, the action

solution: 'Mei Ling' is the one doing the action, so she is the subject.

items.stem: Which voice is used in 'The cake was eaten by the children.'?

explain.why: in the active voice the children would come first, as in 'The children ate the cake'
there are no speech marks or spoken words
'was eaten' is past, not future

solution: The cake receives the action, so the sentence is passive.

items.stem: In 'Hana's bag', what does the apostrophe show?

explain.why: a plural noun is made with 's' and no apostrophe
direct speech is shown with speech marks
here it is not a short form of 'Hana is'

solution: The apostrophe and 's' show that the bag belongs to Hana.

items.stem: In 'The pianist played surprisingly beautiful music.', which word is an adverb?

explain.why: 'pianist' names a person, so it is a noun
'played' is an action, so it is a verb
'music' names a thing, so it is a noun

solution: 'surprisingly' describes the adjective 'beautiful', so it is an adverb.

items.stem: In 'The boy who lives next door is my classmate.', what is 'who lives next door'?

explain.why: it describes the noun 'boy', not a verb
it cannot stand alone as a sentence
a conjunction is one joining word, not a whole group of words

solution: It begins with 'who' and describes the boy, so it is a relative clause.

items.stem: Which tense is used in 'By next June, we will have completed the project.'?

explain.why: 'will have completed' is more than 'will complete'
it is about the future, not the present
it uses 'will have', not 'had'

solution: 'will have' with 'completed' shows an action finished before a future time.

items.stem: What type of sentence is 'If I were you, I would apologise.'?

explain.why: the subject does the action, so it is not passive
it does not order someone to do something
it does not ask anything

solution: It says what would happen under an imagined condition, so it is conditional.

items.stem: Which word is a modal verb in 'You should wear a helmet when you cycle.'?

explain.why: 'wear' is a main verb
'cycle' is a main verb
'helmet' is a noun

solution: 'should' is a helping verb that shows advice, so it is a modal verb.

items.stem: In 'Neither the teacher nor the pupils were ready.', what type of word is 'nor'?

explain.why: 'nor' does not show place or time before a noun
'nor' links two nouns and does not describe a verb
'nor' does not stand in for a noun

solution: 'nor' joins 'the teacher' and 'the pupils', so it is a conjunction.

items.stem: Which of these is a complex sentence?
options: Because it rained, the match was cancelled.
It rained, and the match was cancelled.
It rained heavily and the field flooded.

explain.why: this joins two equal clauses, so it is compound
this has one clause, so it is simple
this joins two equal clauses, so it is compound

solution: It has a main clause and a clause beginning with 'Because', so it is complex.

items.stem: In the sentence 'The brown dog barked loudly.', which word is an adjective?

explain.why: 'dog' is a noun, not an adjective
'barked' is a verb, not an adjective
'loudly' is an adverb, not an adjective

solution: 'brown' is an adjective in this sentence.

items.stem: In the sentence 'The girl sang happily.', which word is a noun?

explain.why: 'The' is an article, not a noun
'sang' is a verb, not a noun
'happily' is an adverb, not a noun

solution: 'girl' is a noun in this sentence.

items.stem: In the sentence 'Siti draws beautiful pictures.', which word is a verb?

explain.why: 'Siti' is a noun, not a verb
'beautiful' is an adjective, not a verb
'pictures' is a noun, not a verb

solution: 'draws' is a verb in this sentence.

items.stem: In the sentence 'The old man walked slowly home.', which word is an adverb?

explain.why: 'old' is an adjective, not an adverb
'man' is a noun, not an adverb
'walked' is a verb, not an adverb

solution: 'slowly' is an adverb in this sentence.

items.stem: In the sentence 'Aunty Lily gave her a gift.', which word is a pronoun?

explain.why: 'Lily' is a noun, not a pronoun
'gave' is a verb, not a pronoun
'gift' is a noun, not a pronoun

solution: 'her' is a pronoun in this sentence.

items.stem: In the sentence 'The cat hid under the sofa.', which word is a preposition?

explain.why: 'cat' is a noun, not a preposition
'hid' is a verb, not a preposition
'sofa' is a noun, not a preposition

solution: 'under' is a preposition in this sentence.

items.stem: In the sentence 'Mei Ling likes tea and Ravi likes juice.', which word is a conjunction?

explain.why: 'likes' is a verb, not a conjunction
'tea' is a noun, not a conjunction
'juice' is a noun, not a conjunction

solution: 'and' is a conjunction in this sentence.

items.stem: In the sentence 'A bird sang loudly.', which word is an article?

explain.why: 'bird' is a noun, not an article
'sang' is a verb, not an article
'loudly' is an adverb, not an article

items.stem: In the sentence 'We flew to Penang last week.', which word is a proper noun?

'week' is a common noun, not a proper noun

items.stem: Which word shows the sentence 'We visited the zoo.' is in the past tense?

explain.why: 'We' is a pronoun and does not show tense

'zoo' is a noun and does not show tense

solution: The verb 'visited' is a past form.

items.stem: Which type of sentence is 'Close the door.'?

explain.why: it does not ask anything
it does not tell a fact
it does not show strong feeling

solution: It tells someone to do something, so it is a command.

items.stem: Which type of sentence is 'What time does the bus leave?'?

explain.why: it does not order anyone to do something
it does not tell a fact
it does not show strong feeling

solution: It asks for information, so it is a question.

items.stem: Which type of sentence is 'The sea is calm today.'?

explain.why: it does not ask anything
it does not order anyone to do something
it does not show strong feeling

solution: It tells a fact, so it is a statement.

items.stem: Which type of sentence is 'How lovely this garden is!'?

explain.why: it does not ask anything
it does not order anyone to do something
it shows strong feeling, which a plain statement does not

solution: It shows strong feeling, so it is an exclamation.

items.stem: Which punctuation mark ends a question?

solution: A question ends with a question mark.

items.stem: Which tense is 'I will visit my cousin tomorrow.'?

explain.why: 'will' and 'tomorrow' look ahead
'will' shows the action has not yet happened
there is no 'have' or 'has' with a past form

solution: 'will' shows the action is yet to happen.

items.stem: Which tense is 'The sun rises in the east.'?

explain.why: 'rises' is not a past form
there is no 'will'
there is no 'was' or 'were' with an '-ing' verb

solution: It states a fact that is always true.

items.stem: Which tense is 'Dad is washing the car.'?

explain.why: 'is washing' shows an action in progress
'is' is present, not past
there is no 'will'

solution: 'is' with 'washing' shows an action in progress now.

items.stem: In the sentence 'She spoke softly.', what kind of word is 'softly'?

items.stem: In the sentence 'Kids love playgrounds.', what kind of word is 'playgrounds'?

items.stem: In the sentence 'The little girl smiled shyly.', which word is an adjective?

explain.why: 'girl' is a noun, not an adjective

'shyly' is an adverb, not an adjective

explain.why: 'was reading' is more than a simple past form
'was' is past, not present
the past perfect uses 'had'

items.stem: Which tense is 'had left' in 'They had left before the rain started.'?

explain.why: 'had left' is more than a simple past form
'had' is past, not present
there is no '-ing' verb

solution: 'had' with 'left' shows an action finished before another past action.

items.stem: Which tense is 'have lived' in 'I have lived here since 2018.'?

explain.why: 'have lived' is more than a simple past form
the past perfect uses 'had'
there is no '-ing' verb

solution: 'have' with 'lived' links the past to now.

explain.why: 'walks' is not a past form

there is no 'will'

items.stem: In the sentence 'The girls quietly entered the hall.', which word is an adverb?

explain.why: 'girls' is a noun, not an adverb

'hall' is a noun, not an adverb

items.stem: In the sentence 'She hid the present beneath her bed.', which word is a preposition?

explain.why: 'present' is a noun, not a preposition

'bed' is a noun, not a preposition

solution: 'beneath' is a preposition in this sentence.

items.stem: What is the subject of 'The smiling baby clapped her hands.'?

explain.why: 'her hands' is the object that receives the action

items.stem: Which sentence is in the active voice?

this is passive

items.stem: Which sentence is in the passive voice?
options: The window was broken by the storm.

this is active

solution: The subject receives the action, so the sentence is passive.

items.stem: In 'Ravi is the tallest boy in his class.', what kind of word is 'tallest'?
